tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.text: The rename worked; GitHub now reports the name as `Orrery`. Running the other 21 renames and updating each local remote URL:

input.command:
cd /c/Users/Yunus-Emre/Desktop/portable_agent_kit; S="C:/Users/YUNUS-~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-Yunus-Emre-Desktop-portable-agent-kit/240bc3b7-3e44-44db-8447-49ccc2b11849/scratchpad"; python - "$S/manifest.json" <<'EOF'
import json, subprocess, sys
m = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
def run(*a, cwd=None):
    p = subprocess.run(a, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=60, cwd=cwd)
    return p.returncode, (p.stdout + p.stderr).strip()
for name, e in m.items():
    owner, cur = e["slug"].split("/")
    new = e["new_name"]
    if cur != new:
        code, out = run("gh", "repo", "rename", new, "--repo", f"{owner}/{cur}", "--yes")
        if code:
            print(f"{name}: RENAME FAILED {out[:150]}"); continue
    url = f"https://github.com/{owner}/{new}.git"
    run("git", "remote", "set-url", "origin", url, cwd=f"projects/{name}")
    code, actual = run("gh", "api", f"repos/{owner}/{new}", "--jq", ".name")
    e["slug"] = f"{owner}/{actual}"
    print(f"{name:<28} {cur} -> {actual}")
json.dump(m, open(sys.argv[1], "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)

# Environment update
 - Primary working directory: C:\Users\Yunus-Emre\Desktop\portable_agent_kit (was C:\Users\Yunus-Emre\Desktop\portable_agent_kit\projects\nomoreclutter)

All four steps are done for the 31 clean repos: renamed, given topics and descriptions, moved to the Aegean 1.1 licenses, committed and pushed. Every repo passed its full AIKit check before its commit.

**Renames:** 22 repos now start with a capital, for example `orrery` → `Orrery`, `prism-relay` → `Prism-Relay`, `aegean-licensing-ops` → `Aegean-Licensing-Ops`. The other 9 were already capitalized. GitHub redirects the old URLs, and the local remotes point at the new names. Local folder names are unchanged.

**Topics and descriptions:** every description is 310 characters or fewer (GitHub's limit is 350) and ends with the license line, e.g. "Free personal use under AL-1.1; commercial use under ACL-1.0." The `agpl`, `mit-license` and `apache-license` topics are replaced with `source-available`, and games also get `drm-free`. No repo has more than 19 topics (limit 20). I read every one back from GitHub to confirm. Orrery's old description was out of date (it said four worlds and terminal only), so I rewrote it from its README.

**Licenses:** 26 repos moved.

| License | Repos |
|---|---|
| AL-1.1 (software) | 20 repos. This includes N1-Engine (was Apache-2.0), NeurologyClinicTemplates-TR (was MIT) and muse (was AL-1.0). |
| AGL-1.1 (games) | Aldervale, Crypt-Crawler, Cyberpulse, Fold |
| ASL-1.1 (science) | PNN (had no license), Obezite-Mekanizma-Projesi |

- **Old-license tags:** each repo's last old-license commit is tagged, e.g. `v0.1.0-agpl`, or `agpl-final` where the repo has no version number. Versions up to and including that tag keep their old license. Repos with a version number moved up one minor version.
- **NeurologyClinicTemplates-TR:** clinics using it for work now need a commercial license. Releases up to `mit-final` stay MIT.

**Fixes that came up along the way:**
- **The three earlier pilots (Assay, Orrery, Prism-Relay):**
  - Their commercial-terms link returned 404 (`blob/main` on a `master` branch).
  - Their history note left out the tagged release itself.
- **Commercial-terms files:** the old AECL/Aegean-E terms are replaced with the current ACL-1.0 template.
- **README length:** three READMEs went over AIKit's 22,500-character limit.
  - **Merklock:** I re-aligned its file tree; no wording changed.
  - **NeuroCore:** I tightened a few sentences without dropping facts.
  - **Cyberpulse:** I moved its 43-command table into a new `COMMANDS.md`.
- **Merklock's rules:** they require a security-review note on every change, so its decision log records one.
- **Aldervale test:** it checked for the old `## License` heading; I changed it to the exact new heading.
- **ASSETS.md:** the game and science repos each got a real inventory instead of the template placeholder.

**On the later list** ([knowledge/repo_backlog.md](knowledge/repo_backlog.md)):
- **Skipped repos:** MemoryReconstruction, voidfarer, fluid-universe, ui-sandbox and AegeanWorks, which had uncommitted work or an open task.
- **AIKit's own license links:** `licenses/CATALOG.md` has the same 404 `blob/main` links as the pilots.
- **AIKit `license --help`:** it still describes the 1.0 licenses.
- **AIKit's README rewrite:** it leaves a blank line inside the file tree and duplicates an existing License section. I fixed the output by hand in every repo, but the AIKit code itself is still unfixed.

**Still open:**
- AIKit itself has 3 local commits for the later list and task record that aren't pushed. I can push them if you want.
- `tmp_pilot_migrate.py` still needs deleting by hand; that was blocked earlier.

I have finished some projects. Look what is left to continue. Also we have no business with AGPL.  Also there is some long descriptions that is out of the limits of Github. Start working. Also look at publish, release tags. We do not have anything to do with those AGPL!
I'll start by re-surveying everything, since some repos may now be clean. I'll also check GitHub-wide for AGPL tags and releases and for any description over the limit.

##### aldervale # aldervale [![Built with AIKit](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-AIKit-6f42c1)](https://github.com/AegeanWorks/AIKit) ALDERVALE - a 2.5D medieval RPG rendered entirely in tiny ASCII cells. Low-poly 3D models (knights, wolves, a walled castle) are baked into shaded character sprites, marched over a voxel heightfield with fog, day/night light, weather and water, and composited with a full RPG on top: quests, combat, loot, shops, saves. It runs in the terminal **and in a browser** through a local canvas thin client over the same Python engine. Standard library only; no dependencies, no assets, no build step. ## 30-Second Cold-Start Quick Reference ##### cyberpulse # cyberpulse [![Built with AIKit](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-AIKit-6f42c1)](https://github.com/AegeanWorks/AIKit) CyberPulse is a retro-cyberpunk terminal hacking simulation game designed around empirical behavioral psychology, featuring procedural puzzle nodes, ICE defense ## ⚡ 30-Second Cold-Start Quick Reference - **Runtime Prerequisites**: Python 3.10+ (standard library only; zero third-party packages required); a modern browser for the Web Cyberdeck. - **Canonical Regression Shield Gate**: ```bash python aikit.py check cyberpulse ``` ##### NeuroOptic # NeuroOptic [![AIKit Integrated](https://img.shields.io/badge/AIKit-integrated-6f42c1)](https://github.com/AegeanWorks/AIKit)

- Document the threat-model consequence of a security-sensitive change in `docs/SECURITY.md`.

## Contribution licensing

Contributions are accepted under AGPL-3.0-or-later, the license of this project. Because Assay is
also offered under a commercial license, the maintainer may require a contributor license
agreement before merging a substantial contribution. Open an issue before starting a large change
so the licensing and design questions are settled first.

====BUSINESS
## Product and packaging

| Tier | Price hypothesis | What the buyer gets |
|---|---:|---|
| Community | free | AGPL-3.0 core: record, ingest, verify, policy review, evidence packs, CLI and library |
| Team | $12k-$24k / year | Commercial license for embedding, policy pack library, priority issues, upgrade guidance |
| Enterprise (roadmap) | $60k-$150k / year | SSO, retention and WORM connectors, key-custody integration, signed head anchoring, private deployment, SLA |
| Design partner | $15k / 6 months | Roadmap influence, two compliance use cases, joint reference pack, named support |
| Readiness service | $15k-$30k | Two-week evidence gap assessment, policy and retention design, auditor-ready sample pack |

The commercial license is for companies that cannot accept AGPL obligations because they embed
Assay in a closed product or distribute it with a proprietary appliance. The verifier and the
open format stay free. That is both the trust story and the distribution strategy.

## Why AGPL-3.0

- Compliance buyers can inspect the integrity rules instead of trusting a vendor's badge.
- A cloud provider cannot take the core, close it and sell it back without contributing or
  buying a commercial license.
- Companies that only self-host internally can use the community edition at no cost, which keeps
  adoption friction low.
- The paid surface is operational: retention, identity, key custody, policy content, support and
  assurance. None of it requires hiding the verification algorithm.
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Cloud observability vendors bundle "audit" features | Win on local-first ownership, offline verification and AGPL trust; integrate rather than compete on dashboards |
| Buyers treat a hash chain as a silver bullet | Publish the threat model, truncation limitation, key custody guidance and anchoring roadmap |

Assay is a local-first evidence layer: a hash-chained ledger, a policy review, and a
self-contained pack that anyone can verify offline. AGPL-3.0 core. Five-minute demo. No account.

## Fifteen-minute demo script
---
force, who approved the exception, and whether the record has been altered.

Today we are releasing Assay, an AGPL-3.0 evidence layer for agent actions. It records tool calls
in a hash-chained JSONL ledger, binds events to a policy digest, reviews the trail for denied
actions and missing approvals, and writes a self-contained evidence pack. Verification is local,
---

Assay is deliberately narrow. It is not a runtime firewall and not a SIEM. It is the evidence
artefact you keep when the dashboard is gone. The core is free under the AGPL today; commercial
licenses, retention/WORM connectors, key custody and support are planned for companies that embed
it in closed products or need an enterprise operating model.
---
2. "A hash chain catches edits. It does not catch a truncated tail or a full rewrite. Assay's
   threat model is public because compliance buyers should know exactly what a control proves."
3. "The verifier is AGPL and the format is documented. If an auditor cannot reproduce the result
   without your SaaS account, it is not evidence."

---
| Subprocessors | None in the community edition |
| Vulnerability disclosure | See `SECURITY.md`; private advisory flow, synthetic reproduction required |
| License | AGPL-3.0-or-later; commercial license available for embedding and enterprise operations |
| Compliance claims | Evidence support only; no certification and no legal advice |

## Objection handling

**"AGPL is a problem for us."**
Use the community edition internally under the AGPL, or buy a commercial license if you embed or
distribute it in a closed product. The verifier and format stay open either way.

**"A hash chain is not tamper-proof."**

file.content:
version = version_of(repo)
    tag = None
    if old:
        tag = f"v{version}-{previous}" if version else f"{previous}-final"
        if not git(repo, "tag", "--list", tag):
            git(repo, "tag", "-a", tag, "-m", f"Last version under {old}")
    apply_license_kind(repo, name, kind)
    history = f"\n> Versions up to and including `{tag}` remain available under {old}." if old else ""
    extra = f" {meta['extra']}" if meta["extra"] else ""
    write(repo / "COMMERCIAL.md", COMMERCIAL.format(free=meta["free"], name=meta["name"], extra=extra,
                                                     history=history, link=LINK), "\n")
    new_version = None
    if version and (repo / "pyproject.toml").is_file():
        new_version = bump(version)
        rewrite_pyproject(repo, meta["key"], new_version)
    elif (repo / "package.json").is_file():
        text, newline = read(repo / "package.json")
        current = re.search(r'"version":\s*"([^"]+)"', text)
        if current:
            new_version = bump(current.group(1))
            text = text.replace(current.group(0), f'"version": "{new_version}"', 1)
        if re.search(r'"license":\s*"[^"]*"', text):
            text = re.sub(r'"license":\s*"[^"]*"', '"license": "SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE"', text, count=1)
        else:
            text = re.sub(r'("version":\s*"[^"]+",)', r'
  "license": "SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE",', text, count=1)
        write(repo / "package.json", text, newline)
    rewrite_readme(repo, meta, old, tag)
    decisions = repo / ".aikit" / "decisions.md"
    if decisions.is_file():
        text, newline = read(decisions)
        lines = [f"## Licensing migration ({tag or '2026-10-26'})", "",
                 f"- New versions use the {meta['name']}" +
                 (f"; versions up to and including `{tag}` remain under {old}." if old else "."),
                 "- Rights holder: AegeanWorks; commercial use under ACL-1.0.",
                 "- Counsel review of the 1.1 texts remains pending."]
        write(decisions, text.rstrip("\n") + "\n\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n", newline)
    print(f"{name}: {meta['short']} tag={tag} version={version}->{new_version}")


for project in sys.argv[2:]:
    migrate(project)

content.text:
The three remaining old-license tags are gone (`mit-final`, `apache-final`, `v0.1.0-al-1.0`), and their history notes are removed from the README and COMMERCIAL.md files of NeurologyClinicTemplates-TR, N1-Engine and Muse. All three passed their checks, then were committed and pushed. No tag or note for an old license is left in any repo. PNN still has its `v1.0.0` tag; that version never had a license, so I left it.

**Should we rewrite git history? I recommend not.**

- **It doesn't take anything back.** Anyone who got a copy under AGPL, MIT or Apache keeps those rights; a license already granted can't be withdrawn. Copies are already out there: NeuralBeat has 2 forks, NeuralDeck and NeuroCore 1 each, and every fork keeps the full history whatever you do to yours.
- **It could hurt you legally.** Rewriting old commits so they show an Aegean license would misstate how that code was actually released. Your own Aegean-Licensing texts are built on the principle that earlier grants aren't revoked, and a falsified history would weaken that position in a dispute.
- **It's disruptive.** It means force-pushing about 35 repos. Every commit ID changes, so every existing clone breaks, along with the kept releases and the decision logs that cite commit IDs. GitHub can also keep serving the old commits by ID for a while afterwards.
- **What matters is already done.** The current code, READMEs, descriptions, topics, tags and releases all show only the Aegean licenses. The old license text is visible only to someone digging through old commits, and that's an accurate record.

If a specific repo really needs a clean slate, for example before selling it, the safer route is a fresh repository that starts from the current code in one commit, with the old one archived. Even then, earlier copies keep their old license.

"""
Project license tiers (ADR-214).

A project `aikit new` creates is in the personal tier: free for personal use under the Aegean
License 1.1 (AL-1.1), with commercial use sold under the Aegean Commercial License 1.0 (ACL-1.0)
in COMMERCIAL.md. A project whose value outgrows free distribution moves to the restricted tier:
its LICENSE becomes the canonical All Rights Reserved notice (`licenses/RESTRICTED-NOTICE.md`)
naming the cutoff commit, COMMERCIAL.md (a public offer) is removed, and
`.aikit/project.json` records the cutoff. A license already granted cannot be revoked, so the
cutoff only looks forward: every version up to that commit stays under the license it carried.
"""

import re
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Optional

from scripts.disruption_recovery import atomic_write_json, file_lock
from scripts.project_publish import run_command
from scripts.project_registry import (
    LICENSE_CHOICES,
    LICENSE_HEADING,
    LICENSES_DIR,
    ProjectError,
    _run_git,
    config_path,
    detect_license_kind,
    license_choice,
    license_header_match,
    load_config,
    reconcile_readme_tree,
    seed_assets_manifest,
    seed_commercial,
    seed_reuse,
    write_reuse_metadata,
)
from scripts.update_knowledge_base import write_generated_file

TIER_PERSONAL = "personal"
TIER_RESTRICTED = "restricted"
# An attached project keeps whatever license it came with; AIKit does not interpret it.
TIER_UNRECORDED = "unrecorded"
RESTRICTED_NOTICE_PATH = LICENSES_DIR / "RESTRICTED-NOTICE.md"
RESTRICTED_LICENSE_HEADER = "AEGEAN RESTRICTED SOFTWARE NOTICE"
RESTRICTED_TREE_LINE = "├── LICENSE                   <- All Rights Reserved (restricted tier)"
# A tree entry is `├──` or `└──` depending on its position, so keep whichever prefix the README
# already uses instead of matching one spelling only (a LICENSE listed last uses `└──`).
_TREE_ENTRY = r"^([├└]──) {} .*$"
_TREE_LICENSE = re.compile(_TREE_ENTRY.format("LICENSE"))
_TREE_COMMERCIAL = re.compile(_TREE_ENTRY.format(r"COMMERCIAL\.md"))
RESTRICTED_LICENSE_SECTION = (
    f"{LICENSE_HEADING}\n\n"
    "All Rights Reserved. This project is in the Aegean restricted tier and is not licensed for "
    "use, copying or distribution; see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for the cutoff commit. Versions released "
    "before the cutoff stay under the license they were released with.\n"
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LicenseState:
    tier: str
    since: Optional[str] = None
    since_commit: Optional[str] = None
    kind: Optional[str] = None
    version: Optional[str] = None

def _triad(what: str, why: str, fix: str) -> str:
    # git output quotes the remote URL, credentials included, so every report is scrubbed (ADR-191).
    return hide_url_credentials(f"Error: {what}\nWhy: {why}\nFix: {fix}")


def _clean_markdown_line(raw: str) -> str:
    """Strip markdown formatting, badges, and html tags from a single line."""
    line = re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", "", raw)
    line = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", line)
    # Strip clickable badges/images: [![alt](img_url)](link_url)
    line = re.sub(r"\[\s*!\[.*?\](?:\(.*?\)|\[.*?\])\s*\](?:\(.*?\)|\[.*?\])", "", line)
    # Strip standalone images and badges: ![alt](url) or ![alt][ref]
    line = re.sub(r"!\[.*?\](?:\(.*?\)|\[.*?\])", "", line)
    # Strip any empty links: [](url)
    line = re.sub(r"\[\s*\](?:\(.*?\)|\[.*?\])", "", line)
    # Replace markdown links [text](url) with text
    line = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\](?:\(.*?\)|\[.*?\])", r"\1", line)
    # Remove markdown formatting characters
    line = line.replace("**", "").replace("*", "").replace("`", "").replace("~~", "")
    return line.lstrip(">*- \t").strip()

        self.assertTrue((science / "REUSE.toml").is_file())

        with self.assertRaises(ProjectError):

    def test_license_suggestion_reads_markers_and_switches_the_pinned_text(self):
        folder = create_project("field-notes", workspace=self.kit, git_start=lambda root: None,
                                description="A small tool for field observations and notes.")
        self.assertEqual(license_state(folder).kind, "software")
        (folder / "data").mkdir()
        self.assertEqual(suggest_license(folder)["confidence"], "low",
                         "one weak marker is not enough to recommend a domain license")
        (folder / "paper.tex").write_text("\\documentclass{article}\n", encoding="utf-8")
        (folder / "CITATION.cff").write_text("cff-version: 1.2.0\n", encoding="utf-8")
        suggestion = suggest_license(folder)
        self.assertEqual((suggestion["kind"], suggestion["confidence"]), ("science", "high"))
        self.assertTrue(suggestion["change_needed"])
        code, out, err = self.run_cli("license", "field-notes", "--suggest", "--json")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        payload = json.loads(out)["result"]
        self.assertEqual((payload["suggested"], payload["recommended_key"]),
                         ("science", "ASL-1.1"))
        self.assertEqual(payload["reasons"], suggestion["reasons"])
        code, _, err = self.run_cli("license", "field-notes", "--json")
        self.assertEqual(code, 2)
        self.assertIn("only meaningful with --suggest", err)
        state = apply_license_kind(folder, "field-notes", "science")
        self.assertEqual(state.kind, "science")
        self.assertTrue((folder / "LICENSE").read_text(encoding="utf-8").startswith(
            "# Aegean Science License 1.1 (ASL-1.1)"))
        readme = (folder / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("Aegean Science License 1.1 (ASL-1.1)", readme)
        self.assertNotIn("Aegean License 1.1 (AL-1.1); see", readme)
        self.assertEqual(license_state(folder).kind, "science")
        self.assertEqual(license_state(folder).version, "1.1")
        self.assertTrue((folder / "ASSETS.md").is_file(), "switching to science seeds the manifest")
        self.assertIn("ASSETS.md", readme)
        self.assertIn("LicenseRef-ASL-1.1", (folder / "REUSE.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertTrue((folder / "LICENSES" / "LicenseRef-ASL-1.1.txt").is_file())
        self.assertFalse((folder / "LICENSES" / "LicenseRef-AL-1.1.txt").exists(),
                         "the old REUSE license copy is removed")
        self.assertIn("REUSE.toml", readme)
        restrict_project(folder, "field-notes", today="2026-10-26", runner=self.git_head())
        self.assertIn("LicenseRef-Aegean-Restricted",
                      (folder / "REUSE.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertTrue((folder / "LICENSES" / "LicenseRef-Aegean-Restricted.txt").is_file())
        self.assertFalse((folder / "LICENSES" / "LicenseRef-ASL-1.1.txt").exists(),
                         "restricting removes the old personal REUSE text")
        with self.assertRaises(ProjectError):
            apply_license_kind(folder, "field-notes", "game")

    def test_a_license_1_0_project_is_still_recognized_and_offered_an_upgrade(self):
        folder = create_project("legacy-app", workspace=self.kit, git_start=lambda root: None,
                                description="A small tool created before the 1.1 texts.")
        shutil.copyfile(ROOT_DIR / "licenses" / "AL-1.0.md", folder / "LICENSE")
        state = license_state(folder)
        self.assertEqual((state.kind, state.version), ("software", "1.0"))

    """`text` (LF) with its first License section replaced by `section` and any later one removed."""
    found = list(_LICENSE_SECTION.finditer(text))

content.text:
I fixed six bugs in AIKit's license and publish tooling and pushed AIKit; all 10 local commits are now on GitHub. All tests and checks pass.

The 7 commits that were already waiting were only docs and task-log updates. The task log looks like it lost entries, but it keeps only the latest 20 by design, so nothing was actually lost.

**Fixes to `aikit license --set` / `--restrict`:**
- **Blank line in the README file tree:** the rewritten LICENSE line no longer leaves an empty line after it.
- **Unlabelled LICENSE line:** a plain `├── LICENSE` line with no comment now gets the license label.
- **Duplicate License section:** a heading such as `## License` or `## 📄 License` is now replaced, and any extra License sections are removed. Before, a second section was added, which is how 7 READMEs ended up with two. Titled sections such as `## Commercial Licensing` are left alone.
- **Help text:** `new --kind` and `license --set` now name the 1.1 licenses.

**Fixes to `aikit publish` descriptions:**
- **Byte-order mark:** a README starting with a hidden byte-order mark no longer makes publish skip the summary (Obezite's case).
- **URL-only paragraph:** a paragraph that is just a link is skipped (NobetWizard's case).
- **Long paragraphs:** text over 350 characters now ends at the last whole sentence, or between words with "…", instead of mid-word (Aldervale's case).

**Catalog links:** 16 links to the license documents returned 404 because they pointed at `blob/main` while the branch is `master`. I fixed them in Aegean-Licensing (pushed) and resynced AIKit's copy.

Each code fix has a new test that failed before the fix. The full test suite (539 unit, 57 integration) passes within its time limits, and so do all the other checks. The decision is recorded as ADR-227.

One item is left on the later list ([knowledge/repo_backlog.md](knowledge/repo_backlog.md)). Aegean-Licensing's draft migration plan (`policies/PORTFOLIO-MIGRATION-PLAN.md`, step 2) still tells maintainers to create a `vX.Y.Z-agpl` tag, which contradicts your no-AGPL decision. It's a policy draft waiting on counsel review, so I didn't edit it. Should I change that step?

def cmd_fix(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """
    Repair what AIKit can repair mechanically, then run the gates: everything left is the
    agent's to fix by hand, guided by each gate's output.
    """
    project = present_project(args.name, args.workspace)
    fixes: List[str] = []
    memory = project.path / ".aikit"
    expected = ["project.json", "guidelines.md", "decisions.md", "task_ledger.json"]
    missing = [name for name in expected if not (memory / name).is_file()]
    write_memory(project.path, project.name, project.test_command)
    fixes += [f"restored .aikit/{name}" for name in missing if (memory / name).is_file()]
    state = license_state(project.path)
    if state.tier == "personal" and state.kind:
        seed_reuse(project.path, state.kind, state.version)
        fixes.append("refreshed REUSE.toml and LICENSES/ metadata")
    if seed_readme(project.path, project.name, project.test_command, integrated=project.attached):
        fixes.append("seeded README.md from the project template (complete it by hand)")
    if migrate_aikit_links(project.path):
        fixes.append("updated the README's pre-move AIKit link")
    fixes += reconcile_readme_tree(project.path)
    fixes += [f"removed stale buffer {rel}" for rel in clean_dangling_temp_files(project.path)]
    if find_python_files(project.path):
        write_generated_file(memory / "codebase_map.md", generate_codebase_map(root=project.path, strict=False))
        fixes.append("regenerated .aikit/codebase_map.md")
    for fix in fixes:
        print(f"[FIXED] {fix}")
    print(f"Checking '{project.name}' after {len(fixes)} repair(s):")
    return cmd_check(args)

def seed_assets_manifest(project_root: Path, kind: str) -> bool:
    """
    Write the asset/data manifest `new --kind game|science` needs, so the license boundary has a
    concrete inventory from the first commit (ADR-223). A software project gets no manifest, and
    an existing file is never overwritten.
    """
    if kind not in ("game", "science"):
        return False
    path = project_root / ASSETS_MANIFEST_NAME
    if path.exists():
        return False
    text = GAME_ASSETS_MANIFEST if kind == "game" else SCIENCE_ASSETS_MANIFEST
    write_generated_file(path, text)
    return True


def write_reuse_metadata(project_root: Path, identifier: str,
                         copyright_notice: str = "2026 AegeanWorks") -> bool:
    """
    Write `LICENSES/<identifier>.txt` and a `REUSE.toml` annotation for `identifier`. The caller
    passes a complete SPDX expression such as `LicenseRef-AL-1.1` (ADR-226).
    """
    try:
        license_text = (project_root / "LICENSE").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        return False
    licenses_dir = project_root / REUSE_LICENSES_DIR
    write_generated_file(licenses_dir / f"{identifier}.txt", license_text)
    metadata = (
        "version = 1\n\n"
        "[[annotations]]\n"
        'path = ["**"]\n'
        'precedence = "aggregate"\n'
        f'SPDX-FileCopyrightText = "{copyright_notice}"\n'
        f'SPDX-License-Identifier = "{identifier}"\n'
    )
    write_generated_file(project_root / REUSE_FILE, metadata)
    return True


def seed_reuse(project_root: Path, kind: str, version: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
    """
    Write the machine-readable REUSE metadata for a project: a `LICENSES/LicenseRef-<key>.txt`
    copy and a `REUSE.toml` annotation naming the current license expression (ADR-226). A project
    that prefers per-file SPDX headers can keep them; this manifest is the baseline. `version`
    keeps a legacy 1.0 project labelled 1.0 instead of the current 1.1.
    """
    choice = license_choice(kind)
    base = choice["key"].rsplit("-", 1)[0]
    return write_reuse_metadata(project_root, f"LicenseRef-{base}-{version or choice['version']}")


def seed_license(project_root: Path, kind: str = DEFAULT_LICENSE_KIND) -> None:
    """Copy the chosen personal Aegean license into a new project (ADR-199, ADR-214, ADR-218)."""
    choice = license_choice(kind)
    source = LICENSES_DIR / choice["source"]
    try:
        text = source.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError as exc:
        raise ProjectError(
            f"Cannot read {source}: {exc}",
            f"a new project starts with the {choice['name']} text AIKit ships.",
            f"restore {source.name} in the AIKit licenses/ folder from git, then retry.",
        ) from exc
    if not text.lstrip().startswith(choice["header"]):
        raise ProjectError(
            f"{source} is not the {choice['name']} text.",
            f"a new project starts with the {choice['name']} text AIKit ships.",
            f"restore {source.name} in the AIKit licenses/ folder from git, then retry.",

    write_generated_file(project_root / "LICENSE", text)

    source = ROOT_DIR / "COMMERCIAL.md"
    try:

def _tree_entry_name(line: str) -> Optional[str]:

    match = re.match(r"^[├└]──\s+(.+?)(?:\s{2,}<-.*)?$", line)

        return None

content.content:
## 4. Commercial Use

Commercial or Organizational Use of a Covered Game is not licensed under AGL-1.1. It needs the
Aegean Commercial License 1.0 (ACL-1.0), evidenced by a certificate that names the project.
Because ACL-1.0 covers software code and logic, Game Assets also need a separate written asset
grant under AegeanWorks' `ASSET_POLICY.md`. Commercial use includes, without limitation:

1. selling, renting or licensing the game, a sequel, a remaster or a derivative game;
2. paid mods, paid asset packs, soundtracks, art books, subscriptions, battle passes,
   advertising-supported builds and in-game purchases;
3. publishing on a storefront under a company, employer or client, or bundling the game with a
   commercial product;
4. operating a paid, public or managed game server whose main value is the Covered Game; and
5. using the game or its assets to train, fine-tune, evaluate or benchmark an AI model, which
   AL-1.1 Section 5.6 already reserves to a commercial license with the `ai-training` Allowance.

Streaming, recording and free fan works under Section 2 are not Commercial Use of the game.

=====
## 5. Commercial and Organizational Use

Commercial or Organizational Use is not licensed under ASL-1.1. It needs ACL-1.0, evidenced by a
certificate that names the project. ACL-1.0 covers software code and logic; Project Data, model
weights and other non-code artefacts also need a separate written grant under AegeanWorks'
`ASSET_POLICY.md`. Commercial use includes, without limitation:

1. use by or for a company, including internal research, production pipelines and client work;
2. industry-sponsored or contract research, clinical deployment, regulatory submission and
   paid consulting;
3. incorporating the Covered Research Material into a commercial product, service, API or
   hosted platform;
4. selling, licensing or redistributing the material or a derivative; and
5. commercial AI training under Section 3.4.

A public research body may use ASL-1.1 under Section 2; a spin-out, commercial arm or
industry-funded project needs ACL-1.0.

def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """
    A display title from a project name: words capitalised, small joining words left lower unless
    first or last, and known acronyms preserved (`muse-ai-music` -> `Muse AI Music`). Only the
    author-facing title is changed; folder names, repository names and descriptions keep their
    spelling (ADR-218).
    """
    words = [word for word in re.split(r"[-_\s]+", text) if word]
    title = []
    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        lower = word.lower()
        if lower in _TITLE_ACRONYMS:
            word = _TITLE_ACRONYMS[lower]

            word = word[:1].upper() + word[1:]
        title.append(word)
    return " ".join(title) or text
